title: Akkadian, the language of the ledger
text:
A merchant from the Levant and a merchant from the Euphrates may share no household tongue, and still write to each other in Akkadian. It is the language of diplomacy and of the account tablet: the language in which a favor becomes a debt with a number attached.

In play, Akkadian opens conversations that would otherwise be gestures, and it improves the price you are offered, because a seller who can explain himself does not need to be cheated.

provenance.notes: Akkadian's use as a diplomatic and commercial lingua franca in this period is well attested.
